title: Absurd: Paul writes about head-coverings yet postpones the chief part of Christian worship
source_text: XIV. Sed, etiamsi Paulus diserte non significaret se jam Corinthiis omnia necessaria tradidisse, quis in animum posset inducere Paulum, quum Corinthiis Evangelium praedicaret, & Ecclesiam apud ipsos constitueret, nihil ipsis tradidisse de sacrificio illo in quo religionis Christianae summa constituenda est, & pars ejus longe praecipua? Et quam praepostera esset ista diligentia Corinthiis scribere de habitu quo viri & feminae debeant in publicis coetibus adesse, in aliud vero tempus differre institutionem de Sacramentis, & eo quod in cultu divino pars praecipua putatur?
pass_a_gloss: But even if Paul did not expressly signify that he had already delivered to the Corinthians all things necessary, who could bring himself to think that Paul, when he was preaching the Gospel to the Corinthians and establishing the Church among them, delivered nothing to them concerning that sacrifice in which the sum of the Christian religion is to be placed, and by far its chief part? And how preposterous would that diligence be, to write to the Corinthians about the dress in which men and women ought to be present in public assemblies, but to put off to another time the institution concerning the Sacraments, and that which is thought the chief part in divine worship?
pass_b_english: Even without 1 Cor 1/15, the timeline is absurd.
Would Paul plant a church and omit the chief sacrificial sum of Christian religion?
Yet he writes now about men's and women's attire in the assembly.
And postpone sacrament institution — Rome's supposed chief part of worship — for later? Preposterous.

rejected: attire now, Mass later is pastoral wisdom
